t: A league of the Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca, joined by the Tuscarora around 1722, under the Great Law of Peace.
Fifty hereditary chiefs, chosen and removable by clan mothers, decided by consensus in a Grand Council at Onondaga.
Strongest Native power of the north-east for over a century, it was split by the American Revolution but its councils still meet.
dyk: The Haudenosaunee issue their own passports, and their national lacrosse team has competed internationally under the confederacy’s flag, the Hiawatha Belt, in a sport they helped to create.
ev: Traditional founding date of the league under the Great Law of Peace (dates debated)
Haudenosaunee war parties destroy the towns of the Huron Confederacy
The Covenant Chain alliance is agreed with the English at Albany
The Great Peace of Montreal ends decades of war with New France
The Tuscarora join, making the Five Nations the Six Nations
The Grand Council covers its fire as the nations take sides in the American Revolution
Joseph Brant leads loyalist Haudenosaunee to the Grand River in Ontario

f.founder: The Peacemaker (Deganawida) and Hiawatha, according to tradition
f.predecessor: The Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca nations
